correctness.rationale: The active inequalities at a filter vertex give the primitive ray generators of its normal cone. Their lattice map is the incidence coboundary with the boundary vertex pinned. The graph is connected: unselected vertices reach the root and its boundary edge, and selected vertices reach selected leaves and their boundary edges. The affine toric divisor presentation applies also to the local ring at the fixed point: all invariant prime divisors on the chart contain it, and an invariant divisor Cartier there has a single character with the prescribed orders on all chart rays. Thus localization does not add relations to the cokernel. The incidence map has a unimodular spanning-tree minor, giving integral H^1, with rank the number of selected leaves minus the number of frontier vertices (also for the empty and full filters). Rank zero means that the rays are a lattice basis; positive rank prevents simpliciality. Root inclusion gives exactly the full filter, and root exclusion separates child subtrees, proving the rank recurrence. The possible nonempty frontier selections on each terminal unary tail are disjoint choices, one vertex per tail, giving the product; the chain and height-zero cases agree separately. The full binary recurrence and inequality follow from M_1=5 and M_h>=M_{h-1}^2. The inspected checker and recorded output are bounded corroboration, not used to infer the theorem or treated as a fresh run.
residual_risks: The proof and decision are for the fixed-point local rings over C, not arbitrary orbit strata or nonnormal variants.

value.rationale: The evaluated integral invariant distinguishes every fixed-point local class group in a natural toric family and shows how branching contributes to its rank. The rank polynomial and leaf-tail product give usable distributions and exact smooth-locus counts without constructing orbit contractions or enumerating all filters. Value is in this combined evaluated classification, not in the standard exact sequence or the elementary binary inequality in isolation.
residual_risks: The scope is this rooted-tree family; no new general toric Cartier criterion is established.
